problem.passage: Art historians have long debated why Dutch still-life painters of the seventeenth century so frequently included wilting flowers, overturned glasses, and half-peeled fruit alongside their most lavishly rendered banquet tables. One common interpretation treats these details purely as moralizing symbols, reminders of mortality inserted to counterbalance the paintings' evident celebration of material wealth. Yet a closer examination of contemporary Dutch trade records complicates this reading: many of the specific flowers depicted, such as tulips and irises out of season, could not have been physically present together at any single sitting, since they bloomed at different times of year and had to be painted from separate studies made months apart. This practical detail suggests that the paintings were never intended as literal records of an actual table at all, but rather as constructed composites designed to display the painter's technical range and, implicitly, the sitter's access to rare and expensive goods across an entire growing season. Read this way, the presence of decay within the image serves less as an isolated moral warning and more as one element within a broader demonstration of abundance, skill, and status that the moralizing interpretation, taken alone, does not fully explain.
problem.stimulus: Art historians have long debated why Dutch still-life painters of the seventeenth century so frequently included wilting flowers, overturned glasses, and half-peeled fruit alongside their most lavishly rendered banquet tables. One common interpretation treats these details purely as moralizing symbols, reminders of mortality inserted to counterbalance the paintings' evident celebration of material wealth. Yet a closer examination of contemporary Dutch trade records complicates this reading: many of the specific flowers depicted, such as tulips and irises out of season, could not have been physically present together at any single sitting, since they bloomed at different times of year and had to be painted from separate studies made months apart. This practical detail suggests that the paintings were never intended as literal records of an actual table at all, but rather as constructed composites designed to display the painter's technical range and, implicitly, the sitter's access to rare and expensive goods across an entire growing season. Read this way, the presence of decay within the image serves less as an isolated moral warning and more as one element within a broader demonstration of abundance, skill, and status that the moralizing interpretation, taken alone, does not fully explain.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Dutch still-life paintings were composed from separate studies of out-of-season flowers because painters lacked access to live floral specimens during the winter months.
The wilting flowers and decaying fruit in Dutch still-life paintings were included solely to remind viewers of mortality, overriding any other purpose the paintings served.
Evidence that these paintings combine flowers from different seasons suggests they were composite displays of wealth and skill, a purpose the purely moralizing interpretation fails to fully capture.
Contemporary Dutch trade records prove that tulips and irises were the most expensive flowers available to seventeenth-century painters and their patrons.
problem.explanation: 지문은 서로 다른 계절에 피는 꽃들이 한 그림에 함께 등장한다는 사실이 그림이 실제 상차림의 기록이 아니라 부와 기술을 과시하기 위한 합성 구성물이라는 것을 시사하며, 부패의 이미지도 이러한 과시의 일부로 재해석되어야 한다고 주장한다. A는 계절이 다른 꽃을 따로 그린 이유를 '겨울철 접근성 부족'으로 잘못 설명하는데, 지문은 이를 인과가 아니라 합성물이라는 증거로 사용한다. B는 전통적인 도덕적 해석을 그대로 반복하지만, 지문은 이 해석이 유일한 목적이 아니라 불완전하다고 명시한다. D는 튤립과 아이리스가 '가장 비싼 꽃'이었다는 근거 없는 주장을 하며, 무역 기록이 실제로 증명하는 바(계절적 불일치)를 벗어난다. 따라서 정답은 C번이다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage argues that the fact different-season flowers appear together in one painting indicates the works are composite constructions displaying wealth and skill, not literal records, and that decay should be reinterpreted as part of this broader display rather than a purely moral message. Choice A wrongly explains the separate studies as due to winter accessibility, when the text uses this fact as evidence of composite construction, not a causal explanation. Choice B simply repeats the traditional moralizing interpretation, which the text says is incomplete, not the sole purpose. Choice D makes an unsupported claim that tulips and irises were the 'most expensive' flowers, going beyond what the trade records actually establish (seasonal mismatch). Therefore, the correct answer is C.

key_relations: the moralizing interpretation (decay as mortality symbol) versus the compositional evidence (out-of-season flowers painted from separate studies)
the seasonal/temporal impossibility of the depicted scene implying the paintings are constructed composites, not literal records
the reinterpretation: decay as one element of a broader display of wealth/skill, not an isolated moral statement
design.answer_uses_relations: The correct choice ties the seasonal evidence to the composite-construction conclusion and to the reframed purpose (display of abundance and skill), showing why the purely moralizing reading is incomplete rather than simply wrong.

distractor_design.relation: the fact that flowers were painted from separate studies
the traditional moralizing interpretation mentioned in the text
the trade-records detail about specific flowers

problem.evidenceTarget: The central idea: seasonal evidence reframes the paintings as composite displays of wealth and skill, complicating the purely moralizing reading of decay.
problem.evidenceSpan: This practical detail suggests that the paintings were never intended as literal records of an actual table at all, but rather as constructed composites designed to display the painter's technical range and, implicitly, the sitter's access to rare and expensive goods across an entire growing season.
problem.answerRationale: 정답은 계절적 불일치라는 증거가 그림을 부의 과시와 기술 과시를 위한 합성물로 재해석하게 하며, 이는 순수한 도덕적 해석만으로는 설명되지 않는다는 지문의 논지를 정확히 종합한다.

difficultyReasons: 정답을 찾기 위해 지문의 여러 문장(계절적 불가능성, 구성적 그림이라는 결론, 재해석된 목적)을 종합해야 함
오답 B는 지문에서 언급된 전통적 해석을 그대로 제시하지만 이는 지문이 비판하는 대상이므로 이를 구분하는 것이 핵심
오답 A와 D는 지문의 세부 근거(사실)를 지나치게 확장하거나 범위를 벗어난 주장으로 만들어 정답과 표면적 정보를 공유함
전체 주장(both interpretations의 통합적 재해석)을 이해해야 정답을 정확히 고를 수 있음

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문에 계절이 다른 꽃들이 따로 그려졌다는 사실 언급이 있어 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.matches: out-of-season flowers, separate studies라는 세부 사실과 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 화가들이 겨울에 생화에 접근할 수 없었다는 원인을 설명하지 않으며, 이는 전체 요지가 아니라 세부 근거의 일부를 잘못된 인과로 확장한 것

distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문 도입부에 언급된 전통적 해석(도덕적 상징)을 그대로 서술하여 익숙하게 느껴짐
distractors.matches: one common interpretation treats these details purely as moralizing symbols
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 이 해석을 반박하거나 불완전하다고 주장하는 것이 핵심이므로, 이 해석이 유일한 목적이라는 진술은 지문의 주장과 반대됨

distractors.plausibleBecause: 튤립과 붓꽃, 무역기록이라는 구체적 세부사항이 언급되어 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.matches: contemporary Dutch trade records, tulips and irises out of season라는 표현과 일치
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 튤립과 붓꽃이 '가장 비싼 꽃'이었다는 주장을 하지 않으며, 무역기록은 계절적 개화 시기를 확인하는 데 사용된 것이지 가격 비교를 입증하는 것이 아님
